summary: Luke Badiali worked on pipeline architecture with Thomas Avery and Grace Lindqvist. CDD mandates move from RFP to decision in days, so a classic long pipeline does not fit. We agreed a pipeline that tracks live deal processes the funds are in, with stages that start before an RFP and clear rules for deals that pause.

discussion.keyPoints: Grace's export showed 84 pitches, 20 won, and a median of 6 days from RFP to decision. Many losses came from deals where the fund dropped out of the auction.
Luke suggested tracking which live processes each fund is in so Brookvale can prepare before the RFP. Thomas said deal partners share this informally over breakfast.
Several mandates were put on hold after phase one red flag work. Grace asked how to treat broken deals in reporting.

recommendations.recommendation: Use five stages: Process watch, Scoping, Pitched, Mandated, Completed, with a scoping call as the exit criterion from Process watch.
Report win rate separately for pitches with and without a scoping call, aiming to restore 35 percent overall.
Hold at least 15 live processes in Process watch at any time across the three sectors.
Close any pitched opportunity with no decision after 21 days as lost, and move broken deals to a separate list.
Measure hours from RFP to pitch submission.

actions.action: Set up the five-stage pipeline and backfill current live processes

nextFocus: Get CRM, data and reporting to support the new pipeline.
nextPreparation: Thomas to confirm which systems hold deal partner contacts today.

tests.question: What are the five pipeline stages?
Is the 15 live processes coverage target agreed?
When do we close a pitched opportunity as lost?
